card.name: Inside drug-interaction sentences
card.fires_on: Commas, small linking words and partway-through-name pieces in drug-interaction sentences, just after a drug or enzyme name and before the effect on another drug. Also seen in a few other lists and numbers.

modes.label: Punctuation or linker after a drug
modes.description: A comma or a word like may or the right after a named drug, before its effect on another drug is stated.
modes.example: Due to potential inhibition of vitamin K activity by methimazole<<,>> the activity of oral anticoagul

modes.label: Inside drug or enzyme names
modes.description: Middle pieces of drug or enzyme names such as CYP2D6, acetaminophen, cilostazol.
modes.example: Coadministration of cilost<<az>>ol with esomeprazole is expected

card.plain: It fires in drug-interaction text at the point just after a drug name, where the sentence is about to describe its effect on another drug.
